o.text: From Russian тире (tire), ultimately from French tiret.

From Proto-Turkic *čadan. Doublet of çiyan.
Cognates
Cognate with Tatar çayan, Bashkir саян (sayan), Kazakh шаян (šayan), Turkmen içýan, Southern Altai сай (say), Turkish çıyan, Kyrgyz чаян (cayan), Uzbek chayon, Uyghur چايان (chayan), etc.
From Proto-Common Turkic *kasïrku. Cognate with Turkish kasırga. Compare Chuvash косӑрка (kos̬ărk̬a, “blizzard”), possibly a Kipchak borrowing.
From Arabic حُرِّيَّة (ḥurriyya). By surface analysis, hürr (“free”) + -iyyət (“-dom; -ness; -ship”).
From hələ + -lik. The interjection is likely a calque of Russian пока́ (poká, “for the time being; bye, so long”).
